subject: first-person Berdly arm orientation corrected to match the stock hand

stock_hand_vbo.note: The stock hand's long axis is Y, and its screen direction runs from the bottom edge to the palm/claws.

axis_evidence.test_0_degrees: Raw Z-long mesh rendered vertically with the claws at the near/bottom end.
axis_evidence.test_90_degrees: R_x(90) mapped the long axis to Y and laid the arm horizontally across the bottom of the frame, ruling out a simple quarter-turn.
axis_evidence.test_180_degrees: R_x(180) kept the long axis vertical, moved the claws to the far/top end and the wrist through the bottom edge, matching the stock arm's visible direction.

live_debug.read_method: GDB read of hypr_hand_debug at RVA 0x6010 in the running process

visual_result.placement: lower centre; wrist leaves the bottom edge, palm and claws point to the far/top end of the gameplay view
visual_result.control_note: Earlier pass-through control shows the stock arm; no game frame is committed.

limitations: The mesh is still static bind-pose geometry; the seven baked actions and feather springs are not applied.
It still samples the game's gold hand atlas; the authored blue feather texture is not bound.
The lower-centre placement follows the stock arm's screen position but has not yet been shifted to a lower-right composition.
The transform is empirically verified in game; the exact hand world/view matrix has not been captured from the executable.
next_step: Preserve this orientation and placement, then bind the authored blue feather material and skin the runtime16 mesh to the baked locomotion actions.
